title: SYSK Selects: What's the deal with Rasputin's death?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode on Grigori Rasputin, the Mad Monk. Josh introduces it as a selected rerun, with a content warning about sexual talk. The hosts cover his birth and early life in Siberia, his religious conversion at a monastery, his association with the Khlysty sect, and his rise to the court of Tsar Nicholas II and Tsarina Alexandra through apparent healing of their hemophiliac son Alexei. They discuss his growing influence during World War I, the political backlash (including Prime Minister Peter Stolypin's failed effort to oust him), the 1914 stabbing by Khionia Guseva, and the conflicting accounts of his assassination by Prince Felix Yusupov and others in December 1916, including the poisoning attempt, the shooting, the body in the Neva River, disputed autopsy findings, the alleged severed penis, the later burning of his body, and a 2000s theory linking British intelligence (SIS) and Oswald Rayner to the fatal shot. The episode ends with a listener mail segment praising the show's editing and producer Jerry, and sign-off.

segments.title: Rerun intro and content warning
segments.summary: Josh introduces this SYSK Selects pick on Rasputin and warns that the episode includes frank talk about sex. Hosts open the episode and tease Rasputin's disputed life.

segments.title: Rasputin's early life and the Khlysty
segments.summary: The hosts describe Rasputin's birth in Siberia in 1869, his marriage and family, and his early religious life. They describe the Khlysty sect and its practices, noting that much of the biography comes from hostile sources and is disputed.

segments.title: Rise to the Romanov court
segments.summary: Rasputin's religious conversion at a monastery, his travels as a healer and preacher, and his arrival in St. Petersburg in 1905, where he was introduced to Tsar Nicholas II and Tsarina Alexandra. He gained favor after apparently easing the suffering of their hemophiliac son Alexei.

segments.title: Political backlash and Russian context
segments.summary: Rasputin's influence grew as Russia moved from agriculture to industry and entered World War I. Prime Minister Peter Stolypin tried to build a case to remove him from court, and the hosts describe rising urban discontent with the tsar.

segments.title: Wartime influence and the 1914 stabbing
segments.summary: With the tsar at the front, Rasputin's allies took government posts during the war, which the hosts say damaged Russia's infrastructure. Khionia Guseva stabbed Rasputin in the stomach in 1914, sent by a former friend, and he survived after surgery and recovery.

segments.title: Assassination by Yusupov and conspirators
segments.summary: The hosts recount the traditional account of Rasputin's murder in December 1916 by Prince Felix Yusupov and others: a poisoned treat that appeared to have no effect, then shots, a beating, and his body dumped in the Neva River. They note the autopsy said hypothermia and that the fatal forehead shot suggests a professional. They discuss Rasputin's own prediction of the family's fate and the Romanov executions.

segments.title: Later theories: British involvement and remains
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the disputed alleged severed penis, the later burning of his body by the Bolsheviks, and a 2000s investigation by a Scotland Yard detective and a historian that linked British intelligence and Oswald Rayner to the fatal shot. They describe a memo and a theory tied to Prime Minister David Lloyd George and the British interest in keeping Russia in the war.

segments.title: Listener mail on editing and Jerry
segments.summary: A listener praises the show's natural conversational feel and the editing work of producer Jerry. The hosts respond that they research separately and have first conversations on mic, with Jerry handling the edits.

segments.title: Outro and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck give social media and email contact details and point listeners to the website for more on this topic.
